aswan-high-dam-nubian-displacement.conditions_add: The Soviet-Egyptian agreement of 27 December 1958 limited the 400 million rouble credit to the cost of Soviet design, survey and research work, Soviet machinery, equipment and materials, and the travel of Soviet specialists, so the money was spent with Soviet suppliers (Article 5). Egypt had to set up a special organisation to manage and finance the construction (Article 3), to pay any cost above the credit by supplying Egyptian goods to the Soviet Union (Article 5), and to credit repayments and interest, and the cost of Soviet specialists in the country, in Egyptian pounds to a separate account at its central bank (Articles 7 and 9). Interest was 2.5 percent a year and repayment ran in twelve equal annual instalments beginning a year after the first stage was finished and the reservoir filled, and no later than 1 January 1964 (Article 6).

why.tied: limited the 400 million rouble credit to the cost of Soviet design, survey and research work, Soviet machinery, equipment and materials, and the travel of Soviet specialists
why.fincov: to pay any cost above the credit by supplying Egyptian goods to the Soviet Union
why.admin: Egypt had to set up a special organisation to manage and finance the construction
why.repay: in Egyptian pounds to a separate account at its central bank

sources_add.title: Agreement on Soviet economic and technical assistance for the first stage of the High Aswan Dam, signed at Cairo 27 December 1958 (with January 1959 covering letter to the Soviet State Bank)
sources_add.publisher: Dams and Modern Egypt (DAME) collection, University of Exeter

aswan-high-dam-nubian-displacement.searched: Left the FRUS cables and went to the agreement text itself: the University of Exeter's Dams and Modern Egypt collection publishes the 27 December 1958 Cairo agreement on Soviet assistance for the first stage, and its Articles 1-9 give the credit limit, interest, repayment schedule, permitted uses, the special organisation Egypt had to create, and the repayment-in-goods and separate-account arrangements.

thilawa-sez-resettlement.conditions_add: JICA's ex-ante evaluation for its Private Sector Investment Finance in the Thilawa Special Economic Zone (Class A Area) Development Project, under an agreement signed on 23 April 2014, says the relocation of the 81 affected households is to be carried out under a "Resettlement Work Plan prepared based on the JICA environmental guidelines", and that the project company Myanmar Japan Thilawa Development Ltd must monitor following the monitoring plan accepted at screening. JICA classified the project as Category A under its 2010 Guidelines for Environmental and Social Considerations.

why.safeguard: the relocation of the 81 affected households is to be carried out under a "Resettlement Work Plan prepared based on the JICA environmental guidelines"
why.admin: must monitor following the monitoring plan accepted at screening

sources_add.title: Ex-ante Evaluation: Thilawa Special Economic Zone (Class A Area) Development Project (Private Sector Investment Finance), Myanmar

thilawa-sez-resettlement.searched: JICA's project pages refuse automated fetching, so went to its evaluation PDFs instead: the ex-ante evaluation for investment project 7150 opens in full and is the appraisal document for the Class A Area investment agreement of 23 April 2014. Note the date: the agreement is dated after the December 2013 compensation agreements with the 81 households, so the plan requirement covers the relocation carried out from 2014 on.

grasberg-freeport.searched: MIGA is retired for this map, so took the other institution in the deal. Opened Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold's FY1995 Form 10-K405 on sec.gov/Archives (filing 0000831259-96-000003): it says only that "FCX maintains political risk insurance that covers a portion of its interest in PT-FI", that "the insurance is primarily designed to cover certain breach of contract risks", that OPIC sought to terminate the US$100 million policy in October 1995 over "environmental concerns about PT-FI's expanded operations", and that Freeport submitted the matter to arbitration; it sets out no requirement attached to the cover. The Austin Chronicle's contemporaneous account quotes OPIC's 10 October 1995 letter on the tailings damage and says OPIC was "likely guided by a 1979 Executive Order", which is a general policy, not a term of this contract. No OPIC contract, term sheet or arbitration award is published.

nyamagasani-hydro.searched: Went past the FMO complaints mechanism's preliminary review to two other document types. The DEG/FMO/Proparco Independent Complaints Mechanism annual report for 2022 (deginvest.de) sets out the eight Nyamagasani complaints, the October and December 2021 mutual agreements and the March 2022 expert panel conclusion, and states no requirement, condition or covenant FMO attached to the financing; the implementation plan and revised grievance mechanism come from the dispute-resolution agreements, not the loan. Frontier Investment Management's own Nyamagasani 1 and 2 briefing (frontier.dk) does not name FMO or the US$39 million facility at all, and says the plants were "developed and constructed in accordance with IFC Performance Standards" without saying a lender required it.

indramayu-coal-jica-farmers.searched: Took the loan-signing document rather than the project page. JICA's own signing notice for the 28 March 2013 Indonesian ODA loan agreements (www2.jica.go.jp/yen_loan/pdf/en/6325/20130328_02.pdf) covers the Indramayu engineering services loan as project (1): 1,727 million yen, 40 years, 10-year grace, 0.01 percent for consulting services, procurement "General untied", and lists no borrower obligation, covenant, land acquisition or environmental requirement. JICA's environmental and social considerations page for the same project gives only the Category A classification and its reason, with the monitoring and remarks fields left blank.

aarey-metro3-car-shed-trees.searched: Took the loan-signing document rather than JICA's project page, which refuses automated fetching. JICA's signing notice for the September 2013 Mumbai Metro Line 3 ODA loan (www2.jica.go.jp/yen_loan/pdf/en/6350/20130918.pdf) gives up to 71,000 million yen, 1.40 percent, 30 years, 10-year grace, 0.01 percent for consulting services and procurement "General untied", names Mumbai Metro Rail Corporation as executing agency, and states no borrower obligation, covenant or environmental requirement. Nothing in it touches the car depot site or tree felling.

uma-oya-tunnel-bandarawela.searched: Went to the borrower government's audit record rather than press accounts. Sri Lanka's Auditor-General's 2016 report on Head 239, Department of External Resources (naosl.gov.lk) covers the project: it gives the financing agreement of 28 April 2008, financing "85 per cent by the Government of Iran and 15 per cent by the Government of Sri Lanka", a cost estimate of not more than US$548.15 million, and says "an Iranian Company had been nominated as the Contractor" without saying the loan required it or how it was chosen. The split of who pays is a financing plan, not a condition. The report does not name the Export Development Bank of Iran and quotes no loan agreement clause.

ramu-nickel-basamuk.searched: Went to the listed partner's own disclosure rather than AidData again. Highlands Pacific's September 2009 ASX corporate presentation (announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20090921) has a "Ramu Finance Structure" appendix giving "China Syndication - US$560M China Exim Bank, US$470M Shareholder loan from the Chinese Syndicate", "Security : Debt funding arranged and secured by MCC", "Non recourse - Non Chinese JV partners have debt portion of capex capped at approx US$950M" and "Repayment: By 2017 from cash flow". Left blank because "arranged and secured by MCC" does not say what secured the facility or that MCC gave a guarantee, and reads equally as MCC having obtained the funding; a later round with the facility agreement could settle it. No conditions precedent, covenant or drawdown requirement is disclosed.

kahuzi-biega-batwa.searched: Went to a later and fuller German government answer (Bundestag printed paper 20/13354) rather than 20/3200. It says payments for Kahuzi-Biega were not suspended ("Zahlungen zugunsten des Kahuzi-Biega-Nationalparks wurden ... nicht suspendiert"), that ICCN and WCS cooperated over the allegations, and in answer to question 29 that KfW's sustainability guideline applies to financial cooperation projects and such requirements are "vertraglich festgehalten" - written into contracts - without naming any term of the Kahuzi-Biega or DR Congo agreements. That is a general policy statement, not a term of this financing. No KfW financing agreement for the 2019-21 bridge payments to ICCN is published.

hambantota-port-zone-clashes.conditions_add: A Johns Hopkins SAIS China-Africa Research Initiative briefing paper that worked from the five Hambantota loan agreements themselves reports that the October 2007 China Eximbank buyer's credit covered 85 percent of the value of the construction contract with the Chinese CHEC-SCL joint venture, with Sri Lanka paying the remaining 15 percent, and that the two September 2012 loans covered about 93 percent of a US$808.1 million CHEC contract, so the money could only be drawn against those contracts. The Government of Sri Lanka was the borrower on all five loans with the Sri Lanka Ports Authority as end-user, and the Treasury "is required to provide the funds to the SLPA for repayments". The paper also states that none of the loan agreements specified the port as collateral and that their event-of-default clauses do not refer to the port.

why.fincov: covered 85 percent of the value of the construction contract with the Chinese CHEC-SCL joint venture, with Sri Lanka paying the remaining 15 percent
why.repay: the Treasury "is required to provide the funds to the SLPA for repayments"

sources_add.title: Briefing Paper: Evolution of Chinese Lending to Sri Lanka Since the mid-2000s - Separating Myth from Reality
sources_add.publisher: China Africa Research Initiative, Johns Hopkins University SAIS

sources_add.title: Special Appendix: Documents Accessed (Hambantota Port Phase I Buyer's Credit Loan Agreement, October 2007; Phase II Government Concessional Loan and Preferential Buyer's Credit, September 2012)
sources_add.publisher: China Africa Research Initiative, Johns Hopkins University SAIS

hambantota-port-zone-clashes.searched: Left AidData and found researchers who had read the agreements. The SAIS-CARI special appendix catalogues the Phase I buyer's credit agreement of October 2007, the September 2012 Phase II concessional loan and preferential buyer's credit, and the ERD repayment schedules; the accompanying briefing paper reports the borrower, the share of each Chinese contract the credit covered, the Treasury's repayment obligation, and that no agreement named the port as collateral. Both files are served from sais-cari.org through a redirect to static1.squarespace.com, which is where the PDFs actually open.

kotopanjang-dam.searched: Went to the full ex-post evaluation rather than the summary and rather than JICA's project pages, which refuse automated fetching. JICA's 2004 full report (jica.go.jp/english/our_work/evaluation/oda_loan/post/2004/pdf/2-06_full.pdf) names the two loan agreements, IP-358 of January 1990 and IP-374 of October 1991, gives the ODA share of cost as 30,025 million yen estimated against 22,810 million yen actual, and repeats that Japan extended the loan on the basis of "the Indonesian commitment to pay sufficient attention to social and environmental impacts" without saying that commitment was written into either agreement. It describes competitive bidding without saying whether bidding was restricted to Japanese suppliers, and sets out no loan condition, special condition or resettlement covenant. The agreements themselves, from 1990 and 1991, are not published.

letpadaung-copper-mine.searched: Fourth attempt. No new document type exists to open: there is no published China Eximbank agreement, no Myanmar parliamentary ratification, no arbitration or court filing quoting the loan, and Myanmar Wanbao's owner NORINCO and partner UMEHL file nothing on an exchange that discloses it. AidData record 64763 still carries the face value and borrowing terms as unknown. A later round would need a leaked or litigated copy of the 2010 facility; nothing published names a term.

namtha-1-dam-resettled-villages.searched: Looked for the concession and offtake side of the deal rather than the loan page. No Lao concession agreement for Nam Tha 1, no China Southern Power Grid International filing and no power purchase agreement with the Golden Triangle or Boten zones is published; AidData has no second record for this project, and AidData 62889, which a search surfaced alongside, turns out to be the Nam Chiane 1 loan, not this one. China Southern Power Grid is not listed, so there is no exchange filing route. No term of the 5 December 2014 China Eximbank loan was found.

nam-ou-cascade-resettlement.searched: Tried the Chinese exchange route this round, since PowerChina is listed in Shanghai: no PowerChina or PowerChina Resources announcement setting out the September 2013 US$660 million China Development Bank facility or the September 2016 US$1.3 billion syndicated facility was found, and no Lao ratification document or concession agreement for the Nam Ou cascade is published. AidData 63762 and 67486 remain the only records and leave collateral, guarantees, escrow and use-of-proceeds unrecorded.

sorik-marapi-gas-leak.searched: Searched in Chinese for an exchange announcement by Zhejiang Kaishan Compressor on the October 2017 US$244.8 million overseas investment loan from China Eximbank and Bank of China; nothing was returned, and the Indonesian and geothermal trade press covers other projects' financings rather than this one. No facility agreement, no Sinosure record and no arbitration filing is published. AidData 62261 remains the only record of the loan.

mirador-copper-mine.searched: Went to the Chinese-language reporting on the banks rather than AidData or the owners' filings. Dialogue Earth's account of the Ecuadorian NGOs' letter to the lenders names Bank of China, China Development Bank, China Eximbank, China Merchants Bank, China Construction Bank and ICBC, and reports the NGOs' argument that the funding breached China's 2012 Green Credit Guidelines, which ask banks to weigh the social and environmental effects of overseas projects. That is a Chinese banking policy, not a term of these loans, and the article says nothing about what the agreements required; none of the six banks replied. No agreement, guarantee announcement or arbitration award setting a term was found.

bisha-mine-forced-labour.searched: Third attempt. The remaining routes are closed: Eritrea publishes no gazette or ratifying law, there is no AidData detail beyond record 56386, and Nevsun Resources' filings describe ENAMCO's purchase of its 30 percent stake without the terms of the China Eximbank loan to the Government of Eritrea that part-funded it. The July 2010 US$60 million follow-on loan has no recorded use. No document naming a term of either loan was found.

tagaung-taung-nickel.searched: Third attempt. The amounts of the June 2007 China Development Bank and China Eximbank support are still unpublished, so there is nothing to find terms for: China Nonferrous Metal Mining Group is unlisted and files no prospectus or exchange announcement on the project, Myanmar publishes no ratification, and no arbitration or court filing quotes an agreement. AidData 34115 records the financing as reported rather than documented.

techo-airport-land.searched: Went to reporting on the operating structure rather than AidData. The Cambodia Daily's account of the airport's opening says the project was developed "in partnership with China Development Bank", that "OCIC holds 51 percent of the project, while the Chinese lender holds 49 percent" and that "China will control the airport for at least 50 years", and gives a US$1.5 billion cost and a separate US$444 million raised by the joint venture from Cambodian and regional banks. It states no amount, tenor, rate, guarantee, collateral or condition for the China Development Bank money. No facility agreement and no text of the January 2018 framework agreement is published.

morosi-obsidian-coal-dust.searched: Went to the lenders' counsel and the trade press rather than AidData. Pinsent Masons' announcement of its work for Bank of China and the syndicate on Xiamen Xiangyu's 2.5 million tonne integrated stainless steel project in Indonesia describes a multi-tiered dual-currency drawdown mechanism in renminbi and US dollars, cover from China Export and Credit Insurance Corporation plus commercial insurance, credit enhancement arrangements across several jurisdictions and an intercreditor agreement, but gives no facility amount, no security package, no use-of-proceeds restriction and no conditions precedent. The Proximo and TXF reports on the same financing are behind subscription and their pages carry only the headline. AidData 92497 names Bank of China as security agent without identifying what secured the loan.

smederevo-hbis-red-dust.searched: Searched in Chinese for an HBIS or Bank of China announcement of the June 2016 US$600 million loan; only Xinhua and other state news accounts of the mill's revival were returned, none of which gives a loan term. HBIS Group is the unlisted parent of the Shenzhen-listed HBIS Company, and no exchange announcement, prospectus or Serbian ratifying law covers this corporate loan - Serbia's Ministry of Finance publishes ratifying laws for state borrowing, and this was not state borrowing. AidData 67013 records no collateral, guarantee, use-of-proceeds restriction or procurement requirement.

pacitan-coal-plant-fishers.searched: Looked for a government guarantee or other security on the China Eximbank loan to PLN, which would be the likeliest term. The Jakarta Post's December 2009 report on the close of financing for the first 10,000 MW programme does not mention Pacitan at all; for the one Chinese loan it does cover, at Tanjung Awar-awar, it says the agreement "is backed by China's state export credit guarantee agency Sinosure" and gives a 13-year maturity with three years' grace at a LIBOR-based rate, and it says only in general that the government would support PLN "through policies and loan guarantees" without tying that to any loan. A World Bank documents API query on the fast track programme and PLN's Chinese export credits returned zero documents. AidData 38610 remains the fullest record and sets out pricing and maturity but no collateral, guarantee, repayment source or tying condition.

cdc-pt-hsl-manis-mata.searched: Went to the UK Parliament's record rather than Down to Earth again, since CDC was answerable to Parliament for this investment. The written answer of 10 April 2000 on the Commonwealth Development Corporation does not mention PT Harapan Sawit Lestari, Indonesia, West Kalimantan or palm oil, and gives only the portfolio-wide rule that "a minimum of 70 per cent of new investments by CDC must be made in poorer countries" - a policy, not a term of this investment. No CDC investment agreement, audit condition or company filing for PT Harapan Sawit Lestari is published.

northern-rangelands-isiolo-conservancies.searched: Looked for the award document itself rather than the evaluation. USAID's grant and cooperative agreement standard provisions (ADS 303 and its mandatory reference) are the general rules that apply to every award of this type, not terms attached to this money, and the brief's rule on general policies excludes them. No copy of cooperative agreement AID-623-A-00-09-00011, and no award modification, audit or close-out document naming a condition on the Northern Rangelands Trust money, is published; the later 2022 award that a search surfaced is a different agreement and cannot be read back onto this one.

haiti-creole-pig-eradication.searched: Went to USAID's own Development Experience Clearinghouse for a project paper, which is the document type that carries conditions precedent and covenants. The one that comes up, PDAAF770A1, is the project authorisation and project paper for African Swine Fever Eradication in the Dominican Republic, project 517-0135, not Haiti: it sets out conditions precedent including "evidence that arrangements have been made for adequate and timely compensation" for depopulated swine, and covenants to hold joint evaluations with A.I.D. and to make the compensation payments. Those belong to a different country's loan and cannot be attached to PEPPADEP. No Haiti project paper or project agreement for the eradication programme is published; the Haitian plan of operations appears only as a library catalogue record with no text.

con-son-tiger-cages-us-aid.searched: Third attempt and no further document type exists. The US General Accounting Office letter remains the only record of the 1971 cell block contract and sets out no condition on the aid; USAID's public safety programme files for South Vietnam are not in the Development Experience Clearinghouse, no project agreement with the Government of Vietnam is published, and the 1970 Congressional Record resolution gives spending figures without a term. A later round would need National Archives holdings of the USAID Office of Public Safety, which are not online.
